title: Angle, Grip, and Forearm Mechanics for Beginner Strumming (Acoustic vs Electric)
summary: This lesson presents beginner strumming mechanics with a focus on relaxed forearm motion, arm placement on the guitar, and pick handling for both acoustic and electric guitars. It emphasizes keeping the arm resting on the guitar to reduce shoulder tension, driving strumming from the forearm rather than the wrist, maintaining a near-parallel hand to the strings, and using a loosely held, thin pick. The instructor then contrasts acoustic and electric setups, noting differences in rest support and comfort, and closes with guidance on adapting mechanics to individual anatomy and instrument size. Practical tips include adjusting pick angle (a slight downward tilt from the thumb), minimizing tension to avoid a harsh sound, and progressive use of thicker picks as control and volume improve.
